worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.summary: Scatters a short-lived, fixed cloud of powder on chosen ground so the caster can walk away. Creatures that step into it and are affected by powder are asked once to turn on the caster; the same individual must wait out a re-entry cooldown before being drawn again. Being a powder, Grass types are immune.
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.use.0: Scatter powder on a retreat path and step away so pursuers walk into it
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.use.1: Pre-place powder on a choke point enemies must pass
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.use.2: Cover a small patch of ground and pin the fight there
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.description: Spread a %1$s block cloud of powder on chosen nearby ground; it stays fixed where it lands instead of following you, lasting up to %2$s. Enemies that just stepped in are redirected to attack you once; Grass types are immune to the powder.

Every %1$s it scans: a newcomer is drawn once, and the same individual must wait %2$s of re-entry cooldown before being drawn again. Staying inside does not keep forcing it, and leaving stops it. The cloud ends when its duration runs out or it is cleared. It works on hostile mobs, not on other players.
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.thick.on: Thick powder: radius x0.85, but re-entry cooldown x1.15 and duration x1.15 - small area, stays longer.
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.thick.off: Thin powder: radius x1.3 (wider), at the cost of re-entry cooldown x0.9 and duration x0.9 (looser).
worldcombat.skill.ragepowder.timing: Scattered on chosen nearby ground; after %1$s s of wind-up it spends %3$s PP, then recovers for %2$s s with a %4$s s cooldown committed on cast.
On (thick): radius x0.85, re-entry cooldown x1.15 and duration x1.15 (small, stays longer). Off (thin): radius x1.3, cooldown x0.9, duration x0.9 (wide, looser).
The companion only powders when a living ally is inside this radius; lower powders only at close range, higher stands up for farther allies.
When an ally falls below this ratio, the powder counts as urgent and goes before ordinary combat; higher is more protective, lower waits until an ally is nearly down.
Below this ratio the companion stops drawing enemies toward itself; lower takes more hits for others, higher protects itself first.
